title: Phase 4b — one bot reader: retire the Go Telegram poller
description: THE DUPLICATION FIX, and the only user-visible behaviour change in the project. One bot token has exactly one reader. internal/operator/telegram/client.go:84 long-polls getUpdates and says so ('a second one gets 409'); cloud/factory/src/telegram.ts registers a webhook and says 'setWebhook and getUpdates are mutually exclusive and the front door is the choice this deployment makes'. They do not collide today only because the Go side has no users. Retire internal/operator/telegram/** (2,171 non-test + 1,852 test) and repoint tk channel and tk tell at the factory's API. telegram/markdown.go goes with the transport; internal/operator/markdownlite.go STAYS (it is the store's formatting, used by the terminal path). MUST land before the move, while both implementations are in one tree and one test run can prove the handover. Consequence to state in the release notes: remote answering now requires a deployed factory; terminal answering is unaffected and still works offline.
notes:
2026-08-28 15:05 - SCOPING CORRECTION FOUND WHILE PLANNING (2026-08-28). This epic's description says 'repoint tk channel and tk tell at the factory's API'. THAT API DOES NOT EXIST.

The factory has /api/channels/telegram/webhook — INBOUND, Telegram calling it. Its outbound helpers (sendTelegramReport, deliverTelegramQuestion) are called internally from index.ts by the run lifecycle; there is no HTTP route a laptop can POST a message to. Grep for a tell/notify/message POST route returns nothing.

So the phase is not 'delete the poller and repoint two commands'. It is 'BUILD the outbound endpoint, then repoint, then delete'. That is a bigger phase than scoped, and building an authenticated outbound message route on a deployed Worker is the part with real design in it — not the deletion.

Also confirmed while checking: internal/operator/telegram is 2,171 non-test lines across four files (channel 756, client 848, factory 460, markdown 107), and cmd/tk/cmd/{channel,tell}.go are 634 + 317. The deletion half is mechanical; the endpoint half is not.
2026-08-28 16:10 - RESHAPED (Peter, 2026-08-28): "should tell/channel live in ticks? ideally ticks have 0 factory couplings."

They should not, and that inverts the phase. My plan an hour ago was to BUILD an outbound endpoint on the factory and point tk tell at it. That would have created a NEW ticks -> factory coupling — precisely the thing the extraction exists to remove — while congratulating itself for deleting an old one.

THE INVERSION, and it needs no new endpoint at all. The CLI surface already exists:
  tk list --awaiting        finds parked questions
  .tick/pending             holds the entries
  tk answer <id> <answer>   resolves one
So ticfac reads parked questions through the tk CLI, delivers them to Telegram, and writes answers back with tk answer. ZERO Go coupling in either direction, and the seam is the CLI — exactly what Phase 1 established. The factory reaches into ticks; ticks never reaches out.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR internal/operator. The split is not "delete the telegram subpackage" — it is one line further in:
  STAYS: PendingStore, Pending, Question, mapping, the parking half of tk ask, tk answer / approve / reject, .tick/pending. Terminal answering, offline, no factory.
  GOES:  internal/operator/telegram/**, AND the Channel interface with its capability interfaces (Adopter, ContextualChannel, FormattedSender, AttachmentSender), AND Consumer in engine.go. Those are the in-process transport extension point, and the CLI replaces them. A Channel interface with no implementation is not a seam, it is a stub.

AND tk tell / tk channel LEAVE. Not "repoint" — relocate. tell.go already exits 4 without a channel and its only channel is Telegram, so it is entirely a remote-notification feature. channel.go is bot-token pairing for a transport that is leaving.

THE ONE CALL WORTH OVERRIDING, so it is on the record rather than assumed: I do not think tk tell needs to survive anywhere. In a terminal-first ticks an agent that wants to tell you something prints it, and anything needing a response goes through the parked-question mechanism. tell exists to reach you when you are AWAY, which is the cloud feature by definition. If you want an equivalent later it is a ticfac command, not a tk one. Say so if you disagree — it changes what gets deleted rather than moved.
2026-08-28 16:23 - tk tell DOES NOT SURVIVE — confirmed by Peter, 2026-08-28. Not relocated to ticfac either. In a terminal-first ticks an agent that wants to say something prints it, and anything needing a response goes through the parked-question mechanism. tell existed to reach a human who is away, which is the cloud feature by definition. Delete it outright.
acceptance_criteria: No Go code calls the Telegram Bot API. No bot token is read from a laptop. Answering from Telegram still resolves a parked question end to end, proven against the fake bot or a live factory. tk answer at a terminal still resolves a parked question with no factory deployed and no network.
closed_reason: Completed: ticks has no Telegram transport, no Channel seam, no tk tell, no tk channel — ~4,000 lines out with no stubs. Delivery moved to a sandbox-side loop reading parked questions through the tk CLI and writing answers back the same way, zero Go coupling either direction. The offline claim is now TRUE and proven: the guard was written BEFORE the change, caught that tk ask/answer silently called a deployed Worker using a credential from the real ~/.ticksrc, and was hardened to assert zero network calls against a POPULATED file rather than an empty temp home. The review verified it by hand with the real binary and a request-logging listener.
